rows.title: The Healing Arc
rows.theme: Ending → Integration → Renewal
rows.authoredText: Death, Temperance and The Star offer a symbolic relationship between endings, integration and hope. If an ending is part of your situation, consider what needs acknowledgment and what a patient pace could look like. Small acts of care may support a steadier orientation without promising recovery or asking you to deny pain. Look to the skeleton on the white horse and banner, Temperance's angel pouring between cups with one foot in water and one on land, and the Star's large star over the pitchers by the pool.

rows.title: The Healing Arc
rows.theme: Ending → Integration → Renewal
rows.authoredText: If grief is part of what you have described, Death can symbolize an ending, Temperance a manageable pace, and The Star the possibility of hope. You might make room for memory and care in ways that suit you, without a timetable for relief or an expectation that loss must become a lesson.

rows.theme: Ending → Integration → Renewal

Consider giving yourself time to acclimate and choosing one manageable practice. The cards do not establish that a transition is underway or predict how it will unfold.

rows.title: The Healing Arc
rows.theme: Ending → Integration → Renewal
rows.authoredText: Releasing old patterns is the work here. Death cuts the cord, Temperance helps you recombine the parts of yourself with compassion, and The Star is the clearer self-image that follows. Name what you are ready to release, and what you are ready to embody.

rows.title: The Liberation Arc
rows.theme: Bondage → Rupture → Freedom
rows.authoredText: The Devil, The Tower and The Sun can connect attachment, disruption and clarity as symbolic themes. If a limiting pattern is relevant, consider what feels restrictive, which assumptions deserve examination and what supports honest expression. Disruption is neither required nor a promise of renewed freedom. The horned figure and chained figures, the lightning-split tower with falling figures, and the radiant sun over the joyful child and sunflowers mirror the release.

rows.theme: Bondage → Rupture → Freedom

You might consider what help would feel useful and one manageable step you choose. The cards cannot establish an addiction, prescribe a rupture or promise recovery.

rows.theme: Bondage → Rupture → Freedom
rows.authoredText: The Devil, The Tower and The Sun can frame questions about attachment, assumptions and clarity in a relationship. rows.title: The Liberation Arc
rows.theme: Bondage → Rupture → Freedom
rows.authoredText: Freedom from limiting beliefs is the initiation. The Devil reveals inherited shame or fear, the Tower breaks the false story, and the Sun returns you to direct experience of truth and joy. Strip the superstition, keep the wisdom, and let your faith become lived.

rows.title: The Inner Work Arc
rows.theme: Solitude → Surrender → Mystery
rows.authoredText: Withdraw to listen (The Hermit). Release the need to force an answer (The Hanged Man). Then move through ambiguity with gentleness—dreams, symbols, and intuition are part of the map (The Moon). This arc rewards patience over certainty. Anchor the inner work in the lantern and six-pointed star, the Hanged Man's halo on the tree, and the Moon's face between the two towers, the dog and wolf, and the winding path.

rows.authoredText: Ideas need incubation. The Hermit protects solitude, the Hanged Man pauses production, and the Moon feeds imagery and myth. Collect fragments, make messy drafts, and wait for the right timing—your creativity is gestating, not failing.

rows.theme: Solitude → Surrender → Mystery

rows.title: The Mastery Arc
rows.theme: Skill → Directed Action → Complete Achievement
rows.authoredText: The Magician, The Chariot and The World connect available skills, chosen direction and integration. Consider which tools you can use, how competing priorities might align and what completion would mean for this task. Reviewing effort and lessons can be useful whether or not the result matches your hopes. The infinity symbol above the wand, cup, sword, and pentacle, the sphinxes beneath the starry canopy, and the World dancer inside the wreath show disciplined motion toward wholeness.

rows.title: The Karmic Acceptance Arc
rows.theme: Fate Turns → Truth Demanded → Surrender to Flow
rows.authoredText: When cycles shift beyond your control (Wheel of Fortune), face the reckoning with honesty (Justice), then release attachment to outcome (The Hanged Man). Acceptance is not defeat—it is wisdom that conserves energy for what you can influence. The turning wheel with the sphinx and snake, the scales and sword, and the Hanged Man's halo on the tree emphasize truth with surrender.

rows.title: Disruption, Hope and Uncertainty
rows.theme: Upheaval → Hope Restored → Navigating Uncertainty
rows.authoredText: The Tower, The Star and The Moon can frame disruption, hope and uncertainty. If change is part of your situation, consider what is known, what remains unclear and what offers a small point of orientation. Intuition can be explored alongside evidence without promising recovery or treating uncertainty as proof. The lightning-struck tower and falling figures, the Star's large star and pitchers by the pool, and the Moon's face between the two towers with the dog and wolf keep the path grounded.

rows.title: The Inner Mastery Through Solitude Arc
rows.theme: Taming Inner Beasts → Solitary Wisdom → Accepting Cycles
rows.authoredText: Gentle self-mastery (Strength) leads to withdrawal for deeper insight (The Hermit), which prepares you to accept the turning of fate with equanimity (Wheel of Fortune). This is the contemplative path: courage, reflection, and surrender to timing. The lion and infinity symbol, the Hermit's lantern on the mountain peak, and the wheel itself mark courage, guidance, and cycles.

rows.title: Journey Stage: Initiation (0-7)

rows.title: Balance and possibility
rows.theme: Balance and possibility
rows.authoredText: Death, Temperance and The Star offer a symbolic relationship between endings, integration and hope. If an ending is part of your situation, consider what needs acknowledgment and what a patient pace could look like. Small acts of care may support a steadier orientation without promising recovery or asking you to deny pain. Look to the skeleton on the white horse and banner, Temperance's angel pouring between cups with one foot in water and one on land, and the Star's large star over the pitchers by the pool.
rows.suppliedText: Patient integration and hope can reinforce each other. Try one manageable adjustment that supports balance, and give a promising possibility room to develop without demanding certainty.

rows.title: Disruption and clarity
rows.theme: Disruption and clarity
rows.authoredText: The Devil, The Tower and The Sun can connect attachment, disruption and clarity as symbolic themes. If a limiting pattern is relevant, consider what feels restrictive, which assumptions deserve examination and what supports honest expression. Disruption is neither required nor a promise of renewed freedom. The horned figure and chained figures, the lightning-split tower with falling figures, and the radiant sun over the joyful child and sunflowers mirror the release.
rows.suppliedText: Disruption and clarity can sit beside each other. If something feels unstable, look for a simple fact or source of warmth that helps you orient; upheaval and recovery are possibilities rather than established events.

rows.title: Perspective and uncertainty
rows.theme: Perspective and uncertainty
rows.authoredText: Withdraw to listen (The Hermit). Release the need to force an answer (The Hanged Man). Then move through ambiguity with gentleness—dreams, symbols, and intuition are part of the map (The Moon). This arc rewards patience over certainty. Anchor the inner work in the lantern and six-pointed star, the Hanged Man's halo on the tree, and the Moon's face between the two towers, the dog and wolf, and the winding path.
rows.suppliedText: A pause and uncertainty can invite a more patient view. Let an unanswered question remain unanswered long enough to consider alternatives, while checking impressions against practical evidence.

rows.title: Direction and integration
rows.theme: Direction and integration
rows.authoredText: The Magician, The Chariot and The World connect available skills, chosen direction and integration. Consider which tools you can use, how competing priorities might align and what completion would mean for this task. Reviewing effort and lessons can be useful whether or not the result matches your hopes. The infinity symbol above the wand, cup, sword, and pentacle, the sphinxes beneath the starry canopy, and the World dancer inside the wreath show disciplined motion toward wholeness.
rows.suppliedText: Direction and integration invite you to connect determined effort with a wider sense of coherence. Ask whether your next step serves the whole project; a completion symbol does not prove an outcome has happened.

Consider which tools you can use, how competing priorities might align and what completion would mean for this task. Reviewing effort and lessons can be useful whether or not the result matches your hopes. The infinity symbol above the wand, cup, sword, and pentacle, the sphinxes beneath the starry canopy, and the World dancer inside the wreath show disciplined motion toward wholeness.
rows.suppliedText: Skill and direction invite purposeful effort. Choose a resource you can use now and a clear next action; focused practice offers a way to test an intention without promising success.

rows.title: Values and choice
rows.theme: Values and choice
rows.authoredText: Growth invites choices: create and nourish what matters (The Empress), decide in alignment with your values (The Lovers), then build a container—commitment, practice, or community—to sustain it (The Hierophant). Notice the wheat fields and Venus symbol, the Lovers' angel between the tree of knowledge and tree of life, and the Hierophant's crossed keys with the two acolytes.
rows.suppliedText: Values and choice invite an honest comparison between inherited expectations and personal commitment. Ask which principle you can stand behind freely; agreement is useful when it preserves agency.

rows.title: Practice and coherence
rows.theme: Practice and coherence
rows.authoredText: Start with a leap (The Fool), apply skill with attention (The Magician), and close the loop with integration (The World). The question is not only "can this be done?" but "who do you become by doing it?" The cliff and white rose, the infinity symbol over the wand, cup, sword, and pentacle, and the World dancer in the wreath frame the cycle.
rows.suppliedText: Practice and coherence invite you to place a useful skill within a broader purpose. Notice what your effort contributes to the whole and what still needs attention; a finished result remains an open possibility.

rows.title: Structure and principle
rows.theme: Structure and principle
rows.authoredText: Create from love (The Empress), then organize your creation with clear boundaries (The Emperor), and finally codify the lessons so they can be passed on (The Hierophant). This arc builds institutions, families, and lasting legacies. The wheat fields and Venus symbol meet the ram heads and orb, then the crossed keys and pillars, to anchor the legacy.
rows.suppliedText: Structure and principle invite thoughtful use of authority. Consider which rule has a clear purpose, who it serves, and how accountability can make a commitment more trustworthy.

rows.title: Fairness and perspective
rows.theme: Fairness and perspective
rows.authoredText: When cycles shift beyond your control (Wheel of Fortune), face the reckoning with honesty (Justice), then release attachment to outcome (The Hanged Man). Acceptance is not defeat—it is wisdom that conserves energy for what you can influence. The turning wheel with the sphinx and snake, the scales and sword, and the Hanged Man's halo on the tree emphasize truth with surrender.
rows.suppliedText: Fairness and perspective invite a measured response. Examine the evidence, consider another angle, and allow time for a careful decision without treating delay as proof of a particular outcome.

rows.title: Hope and uncertainty
rows.theme: Hope and uncertainty
rows.authoredText: The Tower, The Star and The Moon can frame disruption, hope and uncertainty. If change is part of your situation, consider what is known, what remains unclear and what offers a small point of orientation. Intuition can be explored alongside evidence without promising recovery or treating uncertainty as proof. The lightning-struck tower and falling figures, the Star's large star and pitchers by the pool, and the Moon's face between the two towers with the dog and wolf keep the path grounded.
rows.suppliedText: Hope and uncertainty can share the same space. Let a promising possibility guide attention while leaving room for unanswered questions, and check what you sense against what you can observe.

rows.title: Reflection and cycles
rows.theme: Reflection and cycles
rows.authoredText: Gentle self-mastery (Strength) leads to withdrawal for deeper insight (The Hermit), which prepares you to accept the turning of fate with equanimity (Wheel of Fortune). This is the contemplative path: courage, reflection, and surrender to timing. The lion and infinity symbol, the Hermit's lantern on the mountain peak, and the wheel itself mark courage, guidance, and cycles.
rows.suppliedText: Reflection and cycles invite you to notice patterns without treating them as fixed fate. Consider what experience has taught you and which response would fit the conditions you can see now.

variants.title: The Healing Arc
variants.theme: Ending → Integration → Renewal
variants.suppliedText: Death, Temperance and The Star offer a symbolic relationship between endings, integration and hope. If an ending is part of your situation, consider what needs acknowledgment and what a patient pace could look like. Small acts of care may support a steadier orientation without promising recovery or asking you to deny pain. Look to the skeleton on the white horse and banner, Temperance's angel pouring between cups with one foot in water and one on land, and the Star's large star over the pitchers by the pool.

variants.title: The Liberation Arc
variants.theme: Bondage → Rupture → Freedom
variants.suppliedText: The Devil, The Tower and The Sun can connect attachment, disruption and clarity as symbolic themes. If a limiting pattern is relevant, consider what feels restrictive, which assumptions deserve examination and what supports honest expression. Disruption is neither required nor a promise of renewed freedom. The horned figure and chained figures, the lightning-split tower with falling figures, and the radiant sun over the joyful child and sunflowers mirror the release.

variants.title: The Inner Work Arc
variants.theme: Solitude → Surrender → Mystery
variants.suppliedText: Withdraw to listen (The Hermit). Release the need to force an answer (The Hanged Man). Then move through ambiguity with gentleness—dreams, symbols, and intuition are part of the map (The Moon). This arc rewards patience over certainty. Anchor the inner work in the lantern and six-pointed star, the Hanged Man's halo on the tree, and the Moon's face between the two towers, the dog and wolf, and the winding path.

variants.suppliedText: The Tower, The Star and The Moon can frame disruption, hope and uncertainty. The lightning-struck tower and falling figures, the Star's large star and pitchers by the pool, and the Moon's face between the two towers with the dog and wolf keep the path grounded.

review.notes: The creative passage encourages sustained practice despite variable inspiration; its general craft claim does not establish a particular achievement.

variants.title: Journey Stage: Initiation (0-7)
variants.theme: Building Ego & Identity
variants.suppliedText: This stage asks: what are you building, and what identity supports it? Learn your tools, define your values, and practice directed action. The goal isn’t perfection; it’s a stable starting point.

review.notes: The journey-stage passage asks about values, tools and identity without claiming that an absent Major card is drawn.

variants.title: Journey Stage: Integration (8-14)
variants.theme: Shadow Work & Transformation
variants.suppliedText: Here the work turns inward: reality checks, surrender, and transformation. Progress comes from honest reflection, recalibration, and letting go of what can’t continue.

review.notes: The journey-stage language stays broad background about reflection and recalibration rather than importing a particular card or event.

variants.title: Journey Stage: Culmination (15-21)
variants.theme: Shadow Integration & Cosmic Consciousness
variants.suppliedText: This stage brings pressure and insight: attachments are named, illusions fall, and renewal becomes possible. The invitation is to integrate what you’ve learned and carry it back into the world with humility and joy.

review.notes: Renewal remains a possibility and the invitation is reflective; broad journey context is not used as drawn-card proof.

variants.title: The Fool
variants.theme: Beginnings & Open Faith
variants.suppliedText: A new chapter asks for curiosity and lightness. Trust the next step, stay open to surprise, and let learning be part of the path instead of proof that you are behind.

variants.title: Le Mat
variants.theme: Beginnings & Open Faith
variants.suppliedText: A new chapter asks for curiosity and lightness. Trust the next step, stay open to surprise, and let learning be part of the path instead of proof that you are behind.

review.notes: The Fool passage invites curiosity and learning, with no concrete new role, trip or timed outcome asserted.

variants.title: The Magician
variants.theme: Will & Manifestation
variants.suppliedText: You have the tools and the agency to shape this. Clarify your intent, focus your energy, and act with skill instead of hesitation.

variants.title: The Magus
variants.theme: Will & Manifestation
variants.suppliedText: You have the tools and the agency to shape this. Clarify your intent, focus your energy, and act with skill instead of hesitation.

variants.title: Le Bateleur

variants.suppliedText: You have the tools and the agency to shape this. Clarify your intent, focus your energy, and act with skill instead of hesitation.

review.notes: Agency is encouraged without naming resources the user does not possess; intent and a feasible action are practical rather than predictive.

variants.title: The High Priestess
variants.theme: Inner Knowing
variants.suppliedText: The answer is quiet, not loud. Pause, listen, and let intuition surface without forcing it into certainty too soon.

variants.title: The Priestess
variants.theme: Inner Knowing
variants.suppliedText: The answer is quiet, not loud. Pause, listen, and let intuition surface without forcing it into certainty too soon.

review.notes: The Priestess passage explicitly avoids forcing intuition into certainty; no hidden fact or outside person's intent is asserted.

variants.title: The Empress
variants.theme: Nurture & Abundance
variants.suppliedText: Growth comes from care. Nourish what you love, tend the conditions, and let abundance be something you cultivate rather than chase.

variants.title: L'Imperatrice
variants.theme: Nurture & Abundance
variants.suppliedText: Growth comes from care. Nourish what you love, tend the conditions, and let abundance be something you cultivate rather than chase.

review.notes: Care and cultivation remain symbolic Empress themes; no pregnancy, wealth or family circumstance is inferred.

variants.title: The Emperor
variants.theme: Structure & Authority
variants.suppliedText: Stability is built, not wished for. Define boundaries, take responsibility, and build the structure that can hold your plans.

variants.title: L'Empereur
variants.theme: Structure & Authority
variants.suppliedText: Stability is built, not wished for. Define boundaries, take responsibility, and build the structure that can hold your plans.

review.notes: The Emperor passage connects structure with boundaries and responsibility without assigning an authority figure or outcome.

variants.title: The Hierophant
variants.theme: Tradition & Guidance
variants.suppliedText: Wisdom lives in practice and community. Seek counsel, commit to what is meaningful, and let shared values guide your next step.

variants.title: Le Pape
variants.theme: Tradition & Guidance
variants.suppliedText: Wisdom lives in practice and community. Seek counsel, commit to what is meaningful, and let shared values guide your next step.

review.notes: Counsel, community and chosen practice are suggestions, not required obedience or claims of institutional authority.

variants.title: The Lovers
variants.theme: Choice & Alignment
variants.suppliedText: This is a choice about values as much as desire. Align with what you love, be honest about what you want, and choose the relationship or path that fits your integrity.

variants.title: L'Amoureux
variants.theme: Choice & Alignment
variants.suppliedText: This is a choice about values as much as desire. Align with what you love, be honest about what you want, and choose the relationship or path that fits your integrity.

review.notes: The Lovers passage preserves choice and values without declaring an existing romance or a necessary relationship decision.

variants.title: The Chariot
variants.theme: Direction & Determination
variants.suppliedText: Momentum comes from focus. Hold the reins, align competing forces, and keep your direction clear through disciplined action.

variants.title: The Chariot
variants.theme: Direction & Determination
variants.suppliedText: Momentum comes from focus. Align competing forces, keep your direction clear, and sustain disciplined action. This archetype invites deliberate coordination without making a claim about the objects depicted in a particular deck.

variants.title: Le Chariot
variants.theme: Direction & Determination
variants.suppliedText: Momentum comes from focus. Align competing forces, keep your direction clear, and sustain disciplined action. This archetype invites deliberate coordination without making a claim about the objects depicted in a particular deck.

review.notes: The cross-deck Chariot projection removes the literal reins and retains coordinated effort; it explicitly avoids claims about deck artwork.

variants.title: Strength
variants.theme: Courage & Compassion
variants.suppliedText: Real power is gentle. Meet fear with patience, lead with kindness, and let steady courage tame what feels unruly.

variants.title: Lust

variants.suppliedText: Real power is gentle. Meet fear with patience, lead with kindness, and let steady courage tame what feels unruly.

variants.suppliedText: Real power is gentle. Meet fear with patience, lead with kindness, and let steady courage tame what feels unruly.

variants.title: The Hermit
variants.theme: Solitude & Insight
variants.suppliedText: Step back to see clearly. Solitude is not avoidance; it is the space where your inner guidance can become audible.

variants.title: L'Hermite
variants.theme: Solitude & Insight
variants.suppliedText: Step back to see clearly. Solitude is not avoidance; it is the space where your inner guidance can become audible.

review.notes: Temporary reflection is offered as a practice; the passage does not require isolation from support or predict an answer.

variants.title: Wheel of Fortune
variants.theme: Cycles & Change
variants.suppliedText: Life is turning. Notice what is shifting, adapt with flexibility, and use the change to reset a pattern rather than repeat it.

variants.title: Fortune

variants.suppliedText: Life is turning. Notice what is shifting, adapt with flexibility, and use the change to reset a pattern rather than repeat it.

variants.title: Justice
variants.theme: Truth & Accountability
variants.suppliedText: Clarity comes with responsibility. Tell the truth, weigh your actions, and choose the path that restores balance.

variants.title: Adjustment
variants.theme: Truth & Accountability
variants.suppliedText: Clarity comes with responsibility. Tell the truth, weigh your actions, and choose the path that restores balance.

variants.title: La Justice

variants.suppliedText: Clarity comes with responsibility. Tell the truth, weigh your actions, and choose the path that restores balance.

review.notes: Justice remains accountability and balance; the passage does not promise a legal ruling or determine blame.

variants.title: The Hanged Man
variants.theme: Surrender & Perspective
variants.suppliedText: Pause is not failure. Release control, see the situation from another angle, and let the right timing reveal itself.

variants.title: Le Pendu
variants.theme: Surrender & Perspective
variants.suppliedText: Pause is not failure. Release control, see the situation from another angle, and let the right timing reveal itself.

review.notes: The pause is a perspective-taking invitation; no requirement to accept harmful conditions or fixed waiting period is supplied.

variants.title: Death
variants.theme: Endings & Transformation
variants.suppliedText: An ending clears space for the next true thing. Let what is complete be complete, and allow transformation to do its honest work.

variants.title: La Mort
variants.theme: Endings & Transformation
variants.suppliedText: An ending clears space for the next true thing. Let what is complete be complete, and allow transformation to do its honest work.

review.notes: Death is interpreted as symbolic completion and change; no literal death, person or scheduled ending is predicted.

variants.title: Temperance
variants.theme: Balance & Integration
variants.suppliedText: Blend what you have learned with patience and care. Moderation is not smallness; it is the steady rhythm that makes growth sustainable.

variants.title: Art
variants.theme: Balance & Integration
variants.suppliedText: Blend what you have learned with patience and care. Moderation is not smallness; it is the steady rhythm that makes growth sustainable.

review.notes: Temperance supports moderation and integration with no promised treatment outcome or foreign-deck visual claim.

variants.title: The Devil
variants.theme: Attachment & Shadow
variants.suppliedText: Name the attachment honestly. When you see the pattern clearly, you can choose freedom instead of compulsion.

variants.title: Le Diable
variants.theme: Attachment & Shadow
variants.suppliedText: Name the attachment honestly. When you see the pattern clearly, you can choose freedom instead of compulsion.

review.notes: The Devil passage invites examining an attachment; it does not identify a substance, abusive person or diagnosis.

variants.title: The Tower
variants.theme: Disruption & Revelation
variants.suppliedText: Truth breaks through what cannot hold. Let the false fall quickly and rebuild on what is real.

variants.title: La Maison Dieu
variants.theme: Disruption & Revelation
variants.suppliedText: Truth breaks through what cannot hold. Let the false fall quickly and rebuild on what is real.

review.notes: The Tower passage uses disruption metaphor without naming a concrete loss; native and projected meanings agree.

variants.title: The Star
variants.theme: Hope & Renewal
variants.suppliedText: The Star offers hope and gentle care as possibilities. Consider a small practice that supports you or a source of encouragement you might seek, without assuming a prior hardship or promising its resolution.

variants.title: L'Etoile
variants.theme: Hope & Renewal
variants.suppliedText: L'Etoile offers hope and gentle care as possibilities. Consider a small practice that supports you or a source of encouragement you might seek, without assuming a prior hardship or promising its resolution.

review.notes: Hope and care are possibilities with a small practical invitation. No prior hardship or recovery outcome is assumed.

variants.title: The Moon
variants.theme: Uncertainty & Intuition
variants.suppliedText: Not everything is clear yet. Move slowly, respect your instincts, and let the unknown unfold without forcing certainty.

variants.title: La Lune
variants.theme: Uncertainty & Intuition
variants.suppliedText: Not everything is clear yet. Move slowly, respect your instincts, and let the unknown unfold without forcing certainty.

review.notes: The Moon passage preserves uncertainty and cautions against forced certainty; instincts are not treated as proof of hidden events.

variants.title: The Sun
variants.theme: Clarity & Joy
variants.suppliedText: The Sun invites attention to clarity, warmth and enjoyment. You might acknowledge what is working, if anything, and explore what supports honest confidence without requiring yourself to feel joyful.

variants.title: Le Soleil
variants.theme: Clarity & Joy
variants.suppliedText: Le Soleil invites attention to clarity, warmth and enjoyment. You might acknowledge what is working, if anything, and explore what supports honest confidence without requiring yourself to feel joyful.

review.notes: Clarity and warmth retain the Sun's meaning. Acknowledgment of what is working is conditional, and joy is not compulsory or forecast.

variants.title: Judgement
variants.theme: Awakening & Calling
variants.suppliedText: This is a call to rise. Forgive the past, listen for what is asking to be born, and answer with courage.

variants.title: The Aeon
variants.theme: Awakening & Calling
variants.suppliedText: This is a call to rise. Forgive the past, listen for what is asking to be born, and answer with courage.

variants.title: Le Jugement
variants.theme: Awakening & Calling
variants.suppliedText: This is a call to rise. Forgive the past, listen for what is asking to be born, and answer with courage.

review.notes: Judgement is a symbolic invitation to reflection and response; forgiveness is not tied to an invented person or event.

variants.title: The World
variants.theme: Completion & Wholeness
variants.suppliedText: The World invites reflection on completion and integration. Consider what, if anything, feels complete, what remains unfinished and which lessons you want to carry forward. An achievement or transition need not be assumed.

variants.title: The Universe
variants.theme: Completion & Wholeness
variants.suppliedText: The Universe invites reflection on completion and integration. Consider what, if anything, feels complete, what remains unfinished and which lessons you want to carry forward. An achievement or transition need not be assumed.

variants.title: Le Monde
variants.theme: Completion & Wholeness
variants.suppliedText: Le Monde invites reflection on completion and integration. Consider what, if anything, feels complete, what remains unfinished and which lessons you want to carry forward. An achievement or transition need not be assumed.

review.notes: Completion and integration are questions rather than accomplishments attributed to the reader. Unfinished work remains possible.

variants.theme: Transformation clearing into hope
variants.suppliedText: Letting go is not the end of the story. When the clearing is honest (Death), the next phase can be gentler and more inspired (The Star). Focus on recovery, replenishment, and a next true step. The skeleton on the white horse and banner, and the Star's large star and pitchers by the pool, point to renewal after clearing.

variants.theme: Transformation clearing into hope
variants.suppliedText: Letting go is not the end of the story. When the clearing is honest (Death), the next phase can be gentler and more inspired (The Star). Focus on recovery, replenishment, and a next true step. This pairing connects an ending with the possibility of renewed hope.

variants.theme: Transformation clearing into hope
variants.suppliedText: Letting go is not the end of the story. When the clearing is honest (La Mort), the next phase can be gentler and more inspired (L'Etoile). Focus on recovery, replenishment, and a next true step. This pairing connects an ending with the possibility of renewed hope.

review.notes: The dyad makes renewal possible rather than certain and retains the two cards; the cross-deck text removes source artwork.

variants.theme: Transformation clearing into hope
variants.suppliedText: Necessary endings create space for renewal. Grief makes room for healing when you let the ending be real, then tend the recovery with patience. The Star favors gentleness: rest, hydration, honest support, and small rituals that restore faith one day at a time.

variants.theme: Transformation clearing into hope
variants.suppliedText: Necessary endings create space for renewal. Grief makes room for healing when you let the ending be real, then tend the recovery with patience. The Star favors gentleness: rest, hydration, honest support, and small rituals that restore faith one day at a time.

variants.theme: Transformation clearing into hope
variants.suppliedText: Necessary endings create space for renewal. Grief makes room for healing when you let the ending be real, then tend the recovery with patience. L'Etoile favors gentleness: rest, hydration, honest support, and small rituals that restore faith one day at a time.

review.notes: The grief-context source offers ordinary care and support rather than a prognosis; no absent Temperance stage is inserted.

variants.theme: Upheaval revealing clarity
variants.suppliedText: If something breaks, ask what truth it reveals. The Tower strips the false; the Sun restores the simple, bright facts. After the shake-up: simplify, tell the truth, and rebuild from what’s real. The lightning-struck tower with falling figures meets the radiant sun, joyful child, and sunflowers.

variants.theme: Upheaval revealing clarity
variants.suppliedText: If something breaks, consider what truth it reveals. The Tower questions what cannot stand; the Sun favors clarity and vitality. After a disruption, this pairing invites simplicity, honesty, and rebuilding from what is real, without guaranteeing a particular outcome.

variants.theme: Upheaval revealing clarity
variants.suppliedText: If something breaks, consider what truth it reveals. La Maison Dieu questions what cannot stand; Le Soleil favors clarity and vitality. After a disruption, this pairing invites simplicity, honesty, and rebuilding from what is real, without guaranteeing a particular outcome.

review.notes: The opening is conditional and the projection explicitly rejects guaranteed outcomes; native imagery belongs only to the two supplied RWS cards.

variants.theme: Upheaval revealing clarity
variants.suppliedText: The Tower and The Sun can place disruption alongside clarity. If something is changing, consider which facts you can verify, what deserves repair and what routines might support your next step. Change need not be destructive, and difficulty does not guarantee a beneficial result.

variants.theme: Upheaval revealing clarity
variants.suppliedText: La Maison Dieu and Le Soleil can place disruption alongside clarity. If something is changing, consider which facts you can verify, what deserves repair and what routines might support your next step. Change need not be destructive, and difficulty does not guarantee a beneficial result.

review.notes: Disruption and clarity are linked without declaring destruction necessary or joy inevitable. Verifiable facts, repair and routines remain optional useful directions.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: Desire can clarify values, but it can also bind. When attachment tightens (The Devil), choice becomes a test (The Lovers). Name what is hooking you, then choose the path that aligns with your real values. The horned figure and chained figures stand beneath the Lovers' angel between the tree of knowledge and tree of life.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: Desire can clarify values, but it can also bind. When attachment tightens (The Devil), choice becomes a test of values (The Lovers). Notice what holds your attention, then consider the choice that fits your integrity. Attachment and freely chosen commitment are distinct.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: Desire can clarify values, but it can also bind. When attachment tightens (Le Diable), choice becomes a test of values (L'Amoureux). Notice what holds your attention, then consider the choice that fits your integrity. Attachment and freely chosen commitment are distinct.

review.notes: Attachment and values are distinct; the projection avoids asserting a particular coercive relationship while preserving choice.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: When desire mixes with fear, choosing becomes difficult. The Devil highlights compulsion—jealousy, secrecy, obligation, or control. The Lovers asks for a values-based choice: love without chains, honesty over intensity, alignment over attachment.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: When desire mixes with fear, choosing becomes difficult. Le Diable highlights compulsion—jealousy, secrecy, obligation, or control. L'Amoureux asks for a values-based choice: love without chains, honesty over intensity, alignment over attachment.

review.notes: Jealousy, secrecy and control are examples within a conditional relationship discussion, not findings about another person.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: Addiction affects relationship choices. The Devil shows the hook, and the Lovers asks you to choose what supports freedom and health. Seek support, create boundaries, reduce access, and choose the path that strengthens recovery—one honest decision at a time.

variants.theme: Attachment patterns affecting choice
variants.suppliedText: Addiction affects relationship choices. Le Diable shows the hook, and L'Amoureux asks you to choose what supports freedom and health. Seek support, create boundaries, reduce access, and choose the path that strengthens recovery—one honest decision at a time.

review.notes: In the addiction context, support and boundaries are suggestions; the passage does not identify a substance, diagnose the reader or prescribe a treatment change.

variants.theme: Potential meeting capability
variants.suppliedText: Begin with curiosity (The Fool), then act with skill and focus (The Magician). This pairing favors prototypes, experiments, and learning-by-doing—without losing your sense of wonder. The cliff, dog, and white rose, then the infinity symbol over the wand, cup, sword, and pentacle, show potential turning into skill.

variants.theme: Potential meeting capability
variants.suppliedText: Begin with curiosity (The Fool), then act with skill and focus (The Magus). This pairing favors prototypes, experiments, and learning through action, while preserving a sense of wonder. Potential becomes more useful when it meets method and practice.

variants.theme: Potential meeting capability
variants.suppliedText: Begin with curiosity (Le Mat), then act with skill and focus (Le Bateleur). This pairing favors prototypes, experiments, and learning through action, while preserving a sense of wonder. Potential becomes more useful when it meets method and practice.

review.notes: The Fool/Magician dyad supports experiments and skills; the projection removes scenes without losing the practical distinction.

variants.theme: Potential meeting capability
variants.suppliedText: Beginner’s mind is powerful when paired with competence. Take the leap, then choose a method: tools, timelines, and practice. The magic here is follow-through—turn inspiration into a repeatable process and let small experiments become real results.

variants.theme: Potential meeting capability
variants.suppliedText: Beginner’s mind is powerful when paired with competence. Take the leap, then choose a method: tools, timelines, and practice. The magic here is follow-through—turn inspiration into a repeatable process and let small experiments become real results.

review.notes: Method, tools and practice develop the same two-card meaning without requiring an absent completion card.

variants.theme: Bondage meeting disruption
variants.suppliedText: When attachment becomes a trap (The Devil), disruption can be mercy (The Tower). Look for the habit, fear, or story that’s losing power—and choose the freer option, even if it’s uncomfortable at first. The horned figure and chained figures collide with the lightning-struck tower and falling figures.

variants.theme: Bondage meeting disruption
variants.suppliedText: When attachment becomes constraining (The Devil), disruption can expose the pattern (The Tower). Consider which habit, fear, or story is losing its hold and what greater freedom could mean. The pairing invites honest reassessment without predicting a crisis.

variants.theme: Bondage meeting disruption
variants.suppliedText: When attachment becomes constraining (Le Diable), disruption can expose the pattern (La Maison Dieu). Consider which habit, fear, or story is losing its hold and what greater freedom could mean. The pairing invites honest reassessment without predicting a crisis.

review.notes: The conditional source and projection allow reassessment without predicting a crisis; disruption is not asserted to have happened.

variants.theme: Bondage meeting disruption
variants.suppliedText: The Devil and The Tower can invite examination of an attachment and the assumptions around it. If a habit or situation concerns you, consider what you want to understand and which options or sources of support feel appropriate. You can reassess a pattern without being directed to force a crisis or end a relationship.

variants.theme: Bondage meeting disruption
variants.suppliedText: Le Diable and La Maison Dieu can invite examination of an attachment and the assumptions around it. If a habit or situation concerns you, consider what you want to understand and which options or sources of support feel appropriate. You can reassess a pattern without being directed to force a crisis or end a relationship.

review.notes: Attachment and assumptions remain examinable without compulsory crisis or rupture. Reassessment, options and support preserve reader agency.

variants.theme: Cycle turning into a wake-up call
variants.suppliedText: A cycle changes (Wheel) and you’re asked to respond consciously (Judgement). Review what repeats, extract the lesson, and make a deliberate choice that closes the loop. The turning wheel with the sphinx and snake meets the angel's trumpet and rising figures.

variants.theme: Cycle turning into a wake-up call
variants.suppliedText: A cycle changes (Fortune), inviting a conscious response (The Aeon). Review what repeats, consider what you have learned, and make a deliberate choice about how to respond. Changing circumstances and personal accountability can meet without establishing a fixed destiny.

review.notes: The projection ties changing conditions to a conscious response and explicitly avoids fixed destiny; no particular event is supplied.

variants.theme: Cycle turning into a wake-up call
variants.suppliedText: The Wheel and Judgement can connect changing conditions with reflection and conscious choice. If you notice a recurring pattern, consider your part in it, what lies outside your control and whether a different response would fit. variants.theme: Renewed hope calling forth rebirth
variants.suppliedText: Hope returns as a clear signal (The Star). Judgement asks you to answer it: integrate the lesson, release the old story, and rise into the next version of yourself. The Star's large star and pitchers by the pool answer the angel's trumpet and rising figures.

variants.theme: Renewed hope calling forth rebirth
variants.suppliedText: A clear vision is asking to be embodied. The Star is the signal, and Judgement is the decision to answer it. Take one action that matches the future you want: send the message, submit the application, book the appointment, tell the truth.
